# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 53 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 53 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_053_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Similitude 4 is the companion to Similitude 3: where Similitude 3 showed winter (the indistinguishable present age), Similitude 4 shows summer (the age to come when differentiation is revealed). The imagery draws on agricultural eschatology common to Jewish apocalyptic (1 Enoch 10:16-17; 4 Ezra).

The burning of the Gentiles in 53:3 is notable: they are condemned not for sin but for ignorance of the Creator (*ton ktisanta*). This raises questions about natural revelation. The sinners, by contrast, are condemned for sin *and* failure to repent — they had more light.

The personal application in 53:4 echoes Similitude 1's economic critique: wealth-absorption leads to being "found withered" (*xēros*) in the judgment. The term *praxeis* (business dealings) recurs from the Mandates.

EMET's "burned as wood for fuel" preserves the literal Greek (*kaiomenai*); LOGOS/PNEUMA agree. SOPHIA retains this — the firewood image is deliberate (cf. John 15:6).

---

## Similitude 4 — Trees in Summer: The Revelation of the Age to Come

**53:1** He showed me many trees, some with sprouting leaves and some withered. And he said to me: "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, lord," I replied; "some are sprouting and some are withered." "Those that are sprouting," he said, "are the righteous who will dwell in the age to come; for the age to come is summer for the righteous, but winter for the sinners.

**53:2** When therefore the mercy of the Lord shines out, then those who serve God will be made manifest, and all people will be made manifest. For just as in summer the fruit of each tree is made manifest and all are recognized for what they are — so too the fruit of the righteous shall be made manifest and they shall all be known who have been flourishing in that age.

**53:3** But the Gentiles and sinners — as you saw the withered trees — so shall they be found: withered and without fruit in that age, and they shall be burned as wood for fuel and made manifest, because their practice in life was evil. For the sinners shall be burned, because they sinned and did not repent; and the Gentiles shall be burned, because they did not know the One who created them.

**53:4** Bear fruit yourself, therefore, so that your fruit may be made manifest in that summer. And do not be preoccupied with business affairs or entangle yourself in riches of every kind; rather, practice holiness, so that you may be prepared for the summer and not be found withered. For all who are absorbed in business and in wealth will be found withered in that age, unless they are found bearing fruit."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
